subject: Mutual action plan + trial hosting selection for HorizonCX
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@horizoncx.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's discovery

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier — it helped clarify where Redwood could slot into our agent-assist workflow. A few asks from our side to move to a POC:

- Can you share a mutual action plan (MAP) with suggested milestones and owners?
- Recommendations for trial hosting: we want to evaluate Hosted API (fast), Dedicated sandbox (predictable perf), and VPC trial (security-first). Any constraints we should know?
- Success criteria examples and acceptance tests we should run during the trial.
- SOC2 evidence and a short summary we can share with our security team.

We'd like to kick off a two-week technical evaluation in early October and lock a hosting path quickly so our infra team can provision.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Product
HorizonCX

-----Original Message-----

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@horizoncx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery

Elena — thanks for the clear asks, appreciate the urgency. Attached is a first-pass MAP and a short hosting decision memo. High-level summary below; MAP attached as HorizonCX_MAP_v1.xlsx.

Overview (recommended path):
- Short pilot: 2-week technical evaluation (POC) to validate throughput, latency, and output quality on a representative workload.
- Hosting recommendation: Dedicated sandbox for the POC (reserved GPU pool) — gives consistent latency for throughput-sensitive UI flows and lets us mirror production quotas without full VPC setup. If your security team requires customer-managed network or KMS, we can pivot to a VPC trial. Hosted API is fastest to start but may not mirror production perf for your concurrency profile.

Success criteria (examples you can adopt):
- Latency: 95th percentile token-gen latency < 250ms for short requests (<= 128 tokens) under expected concurrency.
- Quality: F1/ROUGE on our 50 prompt testset >= baseline threshold (see MAP tab 'quality-tests').
- Cost/Throughput: sustained throughput >= 40 reqs/sec at median payload with average cost <= $0.02/request (estimate).
- Stability: Zero production-impacting errors for 48h under a replayed traffic profile.

Acceptance tests (run during the 2-week window):
1) Smoke: End-to-end conversation flow with seeded prompts and golden answers.
2) Load: Replay 1 hour of peak traffic across an hour-long ramp to confirm batching behavior.
3) Regression: Run the quality testset and check for model regressions vs baseline.
4) Security check: Verify data retention controls and attestations (SOC2 summary included).

Proposed timeline and owners (short):
- Day 0: MAP accepted + config selection (owner: Elena product; Redwood ops owner: Tessa).
- Day 1–3: Test dataset and sample traffic provided (owner: HorizonCX infra).
- Day 4–5: Dedicated sandbox provisioned + onboarding (owner: Redwood ops / Ben).
- Week 1: Smoke + regression tests (owner: HorizonCX product; Redwood support).
- Week 2: Load and stability tests, handoff notes (owner: HorizonCX product / Redwood SE).

Immediate asks for HorizonCX to unblock (please):
- Confirm hosting preference (Hosted / Dedicated sandbox / VPC trial).
- Provide sample traffic profile (CSV) and a 50-sample prompt set for quality checks.
- Share any must-pass security items (e.g., mandatory KMS, IP table rules).

Attachments referenced: HorizonCX_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with tasks, owners, dates) and Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf (one-page SOC2 extract).

If this looks good I can lock a tentative kickoff slot the week of Oct 4. Ben — added for provisioning questions; Laura — looped for contract/terms if Dedicated is selected.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Adding a few technical clarifications so HorizonCX can choose the right hosting path:

- Traffic profile: please confirm expected concurrent sessions and typical tokens per request. Dedicated sandbox sizing depends on concurrency and sequence length distribution.
- Data sensitivity: if traffic includes PHI, we should default to Dedicated sandbox with optional VPC/KMS. Please flag any fields that must be redacted or excluded from logs.
- Connectivity: for VPC trials we need a CIDR and peering window; for Dedicated sandbox we'll provide a static egress IPs allowlist.
- Model variant: we'll start with the Redwood-verified 'rwd-medium-2026' quantized variant. If you need higher quality, schedule time to test rwd-large-2026 (cost delta noted in MAP).
- Observability: we'll enable token-level traces and a shared dashboard; confirm if you want pre-provisioned Grafana read-only access.

Action items for HorizonCX (technical):
1) CSV with 1k sample requests and traffic histogram (owner: HorizonCX infra).
2) Indicate whether egress IP allowlist or VPC peering is preferred (owner: HorizonCX infra).
3) If SOC2/PHI concerns, share minimal SOU (list of data types in payload).

I can take point on provisioning Dedicated sandbox once we have the sample traffic. Tessa — happy to run the provisioning plan and coordinate the kickoff.

- Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
